_about: Hand-written volcano entries for the globe's Plates & volcanoes layer (scripts/make-layers.mjs volcanoes). They win over NOAA NCEI's Volcano Locations Database and Wikidata, by GVP volcano number. last: a period key (see make-layers) or 'uncertain'. notable: shown on the whole globe too. The build never writes this file.

sources: NOAA NCEI Volcano Locations Database: Tatun Volcanic Group, 25.178 N 121.553 E (its last-eruption code Q: Quaternary, with fumaroles)

Geoscience Letters 2024, 'Volcanic activity around Taipei, Taiwan: new data and perspectives on the Tatun Volcano Group', doi:10.1186/s40562-024-00358-2: new 40Ar/39Ar dating refutes the earlier age model; the date of the last eruption is not settled
Taiwan Volcano Observatory at Tatun (Academia Sinica, Institute of Earth Sciences) watches it
NOAA NCEI Volcano Locations Database: Kueishantao, 24.841 N 121.953 E (code Q: Quaternary, with fumaroles)

Chen Y.-G. et al. 2001, Quaternary Science Reviews, 'A date for volcanic eruption inferred from a siltstone xenolith' (thermoluminescence: possibly younger than 10,000 years, the authors call the date not fully reliable)
Catalogues list eruptions in 1785, 1795 or 1853 from historical accounts, which later studies do not confirm: so 'uncertain'
